study_identification_part.si4_title: Neurodevelopmental model of schizophrenia revisited: similarity in individual deviation and idiosyncrasy from the normative model of whole-brain white matter tracts and shared brain-cognition covariation with ADHD and ASD

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction clearly states the study aim and hypotheses: to map deviations from normative ranges of whole-brain white matter tracts to test similarity and differences among schizophrenia, ASD, and ADHD, using a normative model built from typical controls, and to examine shared cognition–brain covariation.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “We aimed to map deviations from normative ranges of whole-brain major WM tracts for individual patients to investigate the similarity and differences among schizophrenia … ASD … and ADHD.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort comprised 626 typically developing controls recruited from the same community, screened to exclude psychiatric diagnoses, required IQ>70, and underwent MRI quality control excluding scans with low SNR or high signal-dropout counts. Final sample size is reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “…626 typically developing controls (TDC)… All participants had full-scale IQ > 70… We recruited TDC from the same community… interview to exclude any psychiatric diagnoses… Before analysis, the rigorous quality control of MRI data was implemented by excluding those with low signal-noise ratio (SNR) or high signal-dropout counts (SDC).”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Normative models were explicitly sex-specific and modeled GFA as a function of age using the 626 control subjects; data were single-site so no site harmonization was needed.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “Sex-specific WM tract normative development was modeled… from diffusion spectrum imaging of 626 typically developing controls (5–40 years).” / “Individualized tract-deviation profiles comprised GFA Z-scores… derived from the sex-specific normative age models… constructed from 626 TDCs (Male/Female: 376/250; age range 5–40…).”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort data were newly collected at the Department of Psychiatry, National Taiwan University Hospital, scanned on the same 3T Siemens TIM Trio system.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “The three patient groups were recruited from the Department of Psychiatry, National Taiwan University Hospital… and 626 typically developing controls (TDC)… Participants received MRI scans on the same 3-Tesla Siemens TIM Trio scanner with a 32-channel phased-array head coil.”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary imaging acquisition is described with modality, key parameters, and equipment: 3T Siemens TIM Trio, 32-channel head coil, diffusion spectrum imaging with 102 directions and max b=4000 s/mm2 using spin-echo EPI.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: “Participants received MRI scans on the same 3-Tesla Siemens TIM Trio scanner with a 32-channel phased-array head coil. The diffusion spectrum imaging (DSI) protocol… with 102 diffusion-encoding directions with a maximal b value of 4000 s/mm2, using a single-shot spin-echo echo-planar imaging sequence…”

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The paper reports MRI quality control (excluding low SNR/high signal-dropout scans), use of a predefined DSI template with deterministic tractography, and diffeomorphic registration for sampling GFA along 45 tracts, but does not specify preprocessing software versions or full pipeline details.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “Before analysis, the rigorous quality control of MRI data was implemented by excluding those with low signal-noise ratio (SNR) or high signal-dropout counts (SDC)… diffusion profiles… included GFA of 45 major WM tracts… pre-defined on an open-sourced DSI template through deterministic streamline-based tractography… sampling coordinates… transformed from the template to individual MRI datasets with the corresponding deformation maps through diffeomorphic registration.”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative age models were fit using a moving-average approach on all 626 controls with no description of hold-out sets, cross-validation, or other partition-based internal validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “A moving average approach was used to obtain the unbiased mean and variance estimates for the GFA metric in each age range. Next, GFA was transformed into Z-scores, yielding individualized tract-alteration profiles.”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: All analyses use the single-site reference cohort and patient groups; there is no report of applying the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Individualized tract-deviation profiles comprised GFA Z-scores… derived from the sex-specific normative age models… constructed from 626 TDCs… Individual deviations… were then determined for… schizophrenia, ADHD, and ASD.”

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study describes constructing sex-specific normative age models of GFA using a moving-average approach, converting tract values to Z-scores, and using one-sample t tests and F-ratios for deviation and idiosyncrasy assessment.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “Individualized tract-deviation profiles comprised GFA Z-scores… derived from the sex-specific normative age models… A moving average approach was used to obtain the unbiased mean and variance estimates… Next, GFA was transformed into Z-scores… effect sizes of one-sample t-tests… reflect the deviation extent… We used the F-ratio… to estimate idiosyncrasy profiles.”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative fit or calibration metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error) for the normative models beyond describing the modeling procedure.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Not reported; no model fit metrics are provided in the Methods or Results describing the normative model.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning was performed for the normative model; the study used the full reference cohort without train/validation/test splits.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: “A moving average approach was used to obtain the unbiased mean and variance estimates… Next, GFA was transformed into Z-scores…”

nm11_reproducibility.reason: The article does not provide software or library versions or share code/models/data; methods note details are provided elsewhere without offering access or versioning information.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “MRI acquisition, quality control, preprocessing, and tractography are detailed elsewhere [17].”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Eligibility and diagnostic criteria are specified (DSM-IV/DSM-5 schizophrenia, ASD, ADHD), IQ>70 required, exclusions for co-occurring psychotic or neurodevelopmental diagnoses, recruitment site noted, and MRI quality control excluded low-quality scans; sample sizes are given for each subgroup.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “This study recruited 281 patients with schizophrenia… 175… ASD… 279… ADHD… The clinical diagnoses were made by senior psychiatrists per both DSM-IV and DSM-5 criteria… All participants had full-scale IQ > 70… None of the ASD or ADHD participants had any co-occurring psychotic disorders, and none of the schizophrenia participants had a childhood diagnosis of ASD or ADHD… rigorous quality control… excluding those with low signal-noise ratio (SNR) or high signal-dropout counts (SDC).”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses stratified schizophrenia by illness stage based on duration (first-episode, subchronic, chronic) and used age propensity-score matching, but no additional clinical covariates such as medication or symptom severity were modeled.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “The schizophrenia cohort included patients in different stages per the duration-based definition… ‘first-episode’… ‘subchronic’… ‘chronic’…” / “we performed the propensity score weights matching for age… between schizophrenia and neurodevelopmental disorders as the main results.”

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical participants were recruited from a defined site, the Department of Psychiatry at National Taiwan University Hospital, indicating the data source.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “The three patient groups were recruited from the Department of Psychiatry, National Taiwan University Hospital.”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes, ages, illness stage groups, and medication doses for schizophrenia subgroups are provided, with demographic/quality metrics summarized in Table 1.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: “This study recruited 281 patients with schizophrenia (aged 16–40 yrs)… The schizophrenia cohort included patients in different stages… ‘first-episode’… ‘subchronic’… ‘chronic’… (Table 1 and STable 1-2).”

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Diagnostic assessments and cognitive measures are detailed: ASD validated by ADI-R, ADHD by K-SADS-E (and adult supplement), schizophrenia by DSM-IV/DSM-5; neuropsychological tests (CANTAB, Wechsler scales) described in Methods and Supplementary Methods.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: “The clinical diagnoses were made by senior psychiatrists per both DSM-IV and DSM-5 criteria of schizophrenia, ASD, and ADHD. The diagnosis of ASD was validated by the standard diagnostic assessment of the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised… ADHD diagnosis was confirmed by the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia… Neuropsychological functions were assessed by the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB)… and Wechsler intelligence scores.”

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The results interpret the direction of deviation (widespread negative deviations from the age/sex norm) and discuss clinical implications, noting similarity between early-stage schizophrenia and neurodevelopmental disorders and shared cognition–connectivity dimensions, but no explicit quantitative thresholds for atypicality are provided.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “participants with schizophrenia showed widespread significantly negative deviations relative to the age and sex norm in most major WM tracts.” / “we found… the similarity of deviance and idiosyncrasy of WM tracts between early-stage schizophrenia and ADHD or ASD… Using the WM deviation patterns as features, schizophrenia cannot be separated from neurodevelopmental disorders… Moreover, schizophrenia, ADHD, and ASD shared linked cognitive dimensions driven by WM deviations.”
